teile.name: Rule
teile.text: Read the plan before that photo.

regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

Match every visual clip directly to the specific technical step, error state, process execution, or result spoken in the narration.
Use genuine tool interface views and source-backed output examples rather than generic repository overviews, static text blocks, or unrelated UI chats.

Official documentation/help page (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VAST-AI-Research/TripoSR/main/README.md), fetched 2026-11-18.
PAGE TEXT:
# TripoSR This is the official codebase for **TripoSR**, a state-of-the-art open-source model for **fast** feedforward 3D reconstruction from a single image, collaboratively developed by [Tripo AI](https://www.tripo3d.ai/) and [Stability AI](https://stability.ai/). Leveraging the principles of the [Large Reconstruction Model (LRM)](https://yiconghong.me/LRM/), TripoSR brings to the table key advancements that significantly boost both the speed and quality of 3D reconstruction. Our model is distinguished by its ability to rapidly process inputs, generating high-quality 3D models in less than 0.5 seconds on an NVIDIA A100 GPU. TripoSR has exhibited superior performance in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations, outperforming other open-source alternatives across multiple public datasets. The figures below illustrate visual comparisons and metrics showcasing TripoSR's performance relative to other leading models. Details about the model architecture, training process, and comparisons can be found in this [technical report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02151). --> The model is released under the MIT license, which includes the source code, pretrained models, and an interactive online demo. Our goal is to empower researchers, developers, and creatives to push the boundaries of what's possible in 3D generative AI and 3D content creation. ## Getting Started ### Installation - Python >= 3.8 - Install CUDA if available - Install PyTorch according to your platform: [https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) **[Please make sure that the locally-installed CUDA major version matches the PyTorch-shipped CUDA major version. For example if you have CUDA 11.x installed, make sure to install PyTorch compiled with CUDA 11.x.]** - Update setuptools by `pip install --upgrade setuptools` - Install other dependencies by `pip install -r requirements.txt` ### Manual Inference ```sh python run.py examples/chair.png --output-dir output/ ``` This will save the reconstructed 3D model to `output/`. You can also specify more than one image path separated by spaces. The default options takes about **6GB VRAM** for a single image input. If you would like to output a texture instead of vertex colors, use the `--bake-texture` option. You may also use `--texture-resolution` to specify the resolution in pixels of the output texture. For detailed usage of this script, use `python run.py --help`. ### Local Gradio App ```sh python gradio_app.py ``` ## Troubleshooting > AttributeError: module 'torchmcubes_module' has no attribute 'mcubes_cuda' or >

If you don't have an image yet, create one with AI image generation , or describe your idea to 3D Agent . Generate a model from an image To generate a model from an image, follow these steps: In the left sidebar, click Model . At the top of the panel, click the Image to 3D tab. Select High Detail for maximum detail, or Smart Topology for an optimized, game-ready mesh. In the model list, select a model. For High Detail , Meshy 7.1 - Flagship gives the most detail and precision. Under Image , click the upload area, or drag and drop or paste an image. Use a PNG, JPG, JPEG, or WEBP file up to 20 MB. A clear subject on a simple background, at 512 × 512 pixels or larger, gives the best result. Optional: Set the generation options. The panel shows only the options the selected model supports: Multi-view (Meshy 7.1): add images of the same object from other angles. Multi-view needs a paid plan, and free accounts get a limited number of free tries. For more information, see Add views with Multi-view . Resolution (Meshy 7.1): choose how much geometric detail Meshy generates. For more information, see Meshy 7.1 and resolution . Poly Count (Meshy T2): set the target polygon count. Split (Meshy 7.1 and Meshy 6): split the model into parts as part of the generation. You can't turn on Split and Texture together. For more information, see Auto Split .
